\section[il docente]{il docente — the teacher, the lecturer}

\label{lesson:IT-C381-docente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the enrolment, then the Italian for the semester.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il docente}
\textbf{il docente} — \textquotedblleft{}the teacher, the lecturer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il docente risponde alle domande dopo la lezione.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The lecturer answers questions after the lesson.}
\end{quote}

Formal; one form for a man or a woman. In speech, \emph{il professore}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{docente} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{docēns}, present participle of \emph{docēre} \textquotedblleft{}to teach\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il docente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il docente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il docente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the enrolment, then the Italian for the semester, then say \emph{il docente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il docente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The teacher, the lecturer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[il relatore]{il relatore — the thesis supervisor; the speaker (at a conference)}

\label{lesson:IT-C381-relatore}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the semester, then the Italian for the teacher.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il relatore}
\textbf{il relatore} — \textquotedblleft{}the thesis supervisor; the speaker (at a conference)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il mio relatore legge la tesi pagina per pagina.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My supervisor reads the thesis page by page.}
\end{quote}

At a conference, \emph{il relatore} gives a talk.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{relatore} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{relātor} \textquotedblleft{}one who reports, a narrator\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{relātus}, the past participle of \emph{referre} \textquotedblleft{}to bring back, to report\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il relatore}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il relatore}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il relatore}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the semester, then the Italian for the teacher, then say \emph{il relatore} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la borsa di studio]{la borsa di studio — the scholarship, the grant}

\label{lesson:IT-C381-borsa-di-studio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the teacher, then the Italian for the thesis supervisor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la borsa di studio}
\textbf{la borsa di studio} — \textquotedblleft{}the scholarship, the grant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se ho buoni voti, posso avere una borsa di studio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If I get good marks, I can get a scholarship.}
\end{quote}

Literally a purse for study.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{borsa} is inherited from Late Latin \emph{bursa} \textquotedblleft{}a leather bag\textquotedblright{}, from Greek \emph{býrsa} \textquotedblleft{}a hide\textquotedblright{}; \emph{studio} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{studium} \textquotedblleft{}zeal, eagerness, study\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la borsa di studio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la borsa di studio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the teacher, then the Italian for the thesis supervisor, then say \emph{la borsa di studio} again

\section[il dottorato]{il dottorato — the doctorate, the PhD}

\label{lesson:IT-C381-dottorato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the thesis supervisor, then the Italian for the scholarship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il dottorato}
\textbf{il dottorato} — \textquotedblleft{}the doctorate, the PhD\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dopo la laurea vorrei fare un dottorato.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After my degree I would like to do a PhD.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Un dottorato di ricerca} — a research doctorate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dottorato} is built on \emph{dottore}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{doctor} \textquotedblleft{}a teacher\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{docēre} \textquotedblleft{}to teach\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[l'appello]{l'appello — the exam session; the roll call; the appeal}

\label{lesson:IT-C381-appello}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the scholarship, then the Italian for the doctorate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'appello}
\textbf{l'appello} — \textquotedblleft{}the exam session; the roll call; the appeal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se non passo l'esame a giugno, provo all'appello di luglio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If I do not pass the exam in June, I will try at the July session.}
\end{quote}

At school, \emph{fare l'appello} is to call the register.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{appello} is built on \emph{appellare} (EtymDB), a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{appellāre} \textquotedblleft{}to address, to call upon, to call by name\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the scholarship, then the Italian for the doctorate, then say \emph{l'appello} again
